author: Matthew Brown
title: Eagles keep in step blanking Dade County - NewsBreak
text:
By Matthew Brown ,
5 hours ago Riding the momentum of two non-region wins that were by a combined 15-1 tally, Coosa High’s boys soccer team began an important Region 7A D-I stretch of matches Tuesday against a Dade County High Wolverine squad that was on their heels in the league standings.
Ball domination continued to work well for Coosa, and with a focus more on passing than pure speed rushes to the goal the Eagles got the win 4-1 to stand at 2-2 in region play, 8-5 overall. To stay at two losses in 7A D-I when the April 2 home meeting with Dalton Academy arrives, Coosa must go on the road for its next two matches. That includes tonight’s clash with a struggling Christian Heritage club in Dalton, the Lions having only won one match out of 14 all season.
The loss put Dade County at 2-4 in the region.
The Eagles’ first strike on the Wolverines came just over two minutes into play. Carlos Gutierrez won the ball at midfield, Dayton Vicente moved it in the box and Peyton Phillips took the shot. Dade County dodged that strike, but could not handle the physical play of Gabriel Sandoval. He bullied his way towards the net and popped in the first Coosa goal at 36:12.
Sandoval continued to initiate action with a pass to Wallace Ordonez. Ordonez’s shot was blocked, but the Eagles drew a foul after the ensuing throw-in at 32:23. Sandoval took the 29-yard free kick, and the ball went to David Alzate. His shot was deflected for a corner kick taken by Oscar Santillan. That ball was caught by the Dade goalkeeper.
Santillan played a major factor in the Eagle defense denying any long possessions.
With more passing from Phillips to Gutierrez to Henry Rodriguez, Coosa had another shot miss wide at 29:40. Two minutes later Ordonez’s try was blocked; Sandoval recovered the ball but missed himself.
It was Gutierrez, though, who found a breakdown in Wolverine communication at the net. He converted an open shot with 24 minutes left in the first half, and it was 2-0 Eagles.
Less than a minute later, Ordonez took a corner kick for Coosa, and Rodriguez saw his shot saved. Five minutes later, Gutierrez put his head on a corner kick, but Dade was on this save as well. Six minutes later, Alex Vicente, after a feed from Sandoval, hit the top bar. Rodriguez rebounded, shot, but missed wide.
The first action for Alberto Manzalvo as Coosa’s goalkeeper was at 10:55, and it gave Dade its first corner kick. Alzate cleared the ball.
With six minutes left in the half, Coosa’s next corner try went to Ordonez, but his shot was saved. Rodriguez was denied in goal at 2:37. Otherwise, with all the passing, the Eagles lost a few more shot attempts from the offsides whistle.
To start the second half, at 34;25, Sandoval and Gutierrez worked together inside for a blocked shot. A minute later the Wolverines took a long free kick into the Eagle box, but Dade County fouled Manzalvo, who had to be tended to and removed from play. He did return.
At 30:29, Ordonez drew a foul for a penalty kick that he connected on for 3-0 Eagles. Gutierrez scored a second time for Coosa. Vicente missed one from a Santillan pass at 25:50.
It was a frustrating night, though, for the Coosa High girls soccer team looking to end a four-match losing streak. Instead, Dade County scored twice in the second half and protected the lead with smothering defense, the final 2-0.
The Lady Eagles dropped to 5-7 overall, 1-3 in 7A D-I.
Dade’s girls snatched the lead early in the second half, then Coosa goalkeeper Abigail Johnson recorded saves at 33:22 and 32:25. Lexi Day helped her with a sliding stop at 27:10, then Jobie Ordonez and Kinsley Lovely worked the ball up against a multitude of defenders for a wide miss.
Lovely, with under 19 minutes to play, was able to stay onside while being chased by Dade players, and her shot hit the right post. She missed again wide after a steal by Ordonez.
Coosa also had a 20-yard free kick that lifted too high. Day attempted to even out numbers playing upfield, and Sarah Kate Kelley won numerous 50-50 midfield balls for the hosts. Time was running short, however, and when Ordonez drew another foul at 7:50, Day hit a 40-yarder right to the keeper.
It then became a sideline battle near the benches. As the ball got back in more open territory, Dade County worked a cross-to-cross connection to score goal No. 2 at 4:02.
Also in soccer action Tuesday, Darlington’s boys and girls teams demolished Haralson County at home, 11-1 and 8-0 respectively. George Loveless had three goals plus an assist in the boys contest. The Tigers next play at Temple High in Carroll County on Friday.
Rome High, in bids to win Region 5-5A championships, shut out Lithia Springs on the road, 4-0 for the boys and 9-0 for the girls. Daniella and Isabella Sanchez each scored twice in the girls contest.
